qti-assessment-test.title: Beacon Hill Financial Educators - Form 1040 Schedule C Passive Loss & Private Equity Waterfall CPE (QAS Self-Study Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Compute the allowable IRC Sec. 469(i) rental real estate loss deduction after MAGI phase-out on Form 1040.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Compute the allowable IRC Sec. 469(i) rental real estate loss deduction after MAGI phase-out on Form 1040.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A married couple filing jointly actively participates in a residential rental property generating a $22,000 net passive loss and reports Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) of $128,000 (with no other passive income and neither spouse qualifying as a real estate professional). How much of the rental loss may offset nonpassive W-2 wages in the current tax year?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: $11,000 deductible on Schedule E; the remaining $11,000 passive loss is suspended on Form 8582 and carried forward.
$22,000 deductible in full because total MAGI remains below the $150,000 complete phase-out ceiling.
$8,000 deductible because the $28,000 excess MAGI reduces the $22,000 actual rental loss dollar-for-dollar above $114,000.
$0 deductible unless at least one spouse logs 750 hours under IRC Sec. 469(c)(7).

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Excess MAGI over $100,000 is $28,000; 50% of $28,000 reduces the $25,000 cap by $14,000 to an $11,000 maximum allowance, suspending the remaining $11,000.
Incorrect. The $25,000 allowance phases out ratably by 50 cents per dollar of MAGI between $100,000 and $150,000 rather than dropping off as a cliff at $150,000.
Incorrect. The 50% phase-out reduces the $25,000 statutory cap first, not the taxpayer's $22,000 realized loss.
Incorrect. Active participation (a lower standard than the 750-hour real estate professional test) qualifies taxpayers with MAGI below $150,000 for the partial Sec. 469(i) allowance.

qti-assessment-item.title: Distinguish European whole-fund distribution waterfalls from American deal-by-deal carry mechanics.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Distinguish European whole-fund distribution waterfalls from American deal-by-deal carry mechanics.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During due diligence for a CFP/CPA client evaluating a private equity fund with an 8% preferred hurdle and 20% carried interest, why does a European whole-fund waterfall expose Limited Partners to lower clawback risk than an American deal-by-deal waterfall?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The General Partner receives zero carried interest until LPs recover 100% of aggregate contributed capital (including unexited investments and fees) plus the 8% hurdle across the entire fund.
European waterfalls prohibit GP catch-up tranches and cap lifetime carried interest at 8% of net realized gains.
European waterfalls tax all GP carried interest at ordinary IRC Sec. 1061 short-term rates regardless of holding period.
American waterfalls defer all LP distributions until final fund liquidation in Year 10.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Returning all contributed capital and preferred return at the whole-fund level prevents early deal-level carry overpayments when later portfolio exits underperform.
Incorrect. European waterfalls routinely include an 80/20 or 100% GP catch-up tranche once whole-fund capital and the 8% LP hurdle have been returned.
Incorrect. Waterfall priority governs LP/GP cash distribution timing, whereas IRC Sec. 1061 governs the three-year holding period for long-term capital gain treatment.
Incorrect. Both waterfall structures distribute proceeds upon exits; American waterfalls pay GP carry per deal prior to full fund-level capital recovery.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply NASBA QAS Self-Study and Circular 230 conflict-of-interest standards in CPA tax engagements.

qti-item-body.p: Objective: Apply NASBA QAS Self-Study and Circular 230 conflict-of-interest standards in CPA tax engagements.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Two equal LLC members ask their CPA to prepare both partners' personal Form 1040 returns while advocating opposing purchase-price allocations under IRC Sec. 1060 during a buyout. Under Treasury Circular 230 Sec. 10.29, when may the CPA represent both taxpayers?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Only if the CPA reasonably believes competent and diligent representation can be provided to each affected client, the representation is not prohibited by law, and each client gives informed written consent within 30 days.
Immediately upon recording oral consent in the workpapers, provided both clients receive identical hourly billing rates.
Whenever the LLC operating agreement names the CPA as tax matters representative, overriding individual consent rules.
Never under any circumstance, even when the allocation terms are already fixed and both clients sign written waivers.

qti-content-body.p: Correct. Circular 230 Sec. 10.29 requires objective competence belief, legality, and signed informed consent from each affected client confirmed in writing within 30 days (retained for 36 months).
Incorrect. Circular 230 Sec. 10.29(b)(3) strictly requires each affected client to waive the conflict via informed consent confirmed in writing.
Incorrect. Entity-level engagement clauses do not waive an active conflict between adverse individual Form 1040 clients without separate informed written consents.
Incorrect. Circular 230 permits waivable conflicts when competent representation remains feasible and timely written informed consents are obtained.
